sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r3/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: 'Quality Checks' row 32 (check #31) and 'Internal Quality Checks' row 32 (check #31); the workbook package has no cell comments or notes
qc/runs/kittle-2026-10-09-r3/raw-evidence-index.json (all 6 artifact hashes and their matching source hashes re-verified: all match)
qc/repairs/kittle-2026-10-08/results/functional-before.json, functional-after.json, golden-run.log; tests/functional.cjs (exact-count and order assertions)
evidence: Scope: every every/all/only/exactly-once/each/any/unchanged wording in the 16 functional, 5 polish, 4 visual and 2 gate criteria, checked against the seed and the run order. test.sh runs the gates, then the scored suites, with --max-concurrent-agent 1; functional runs in individual mode on one shared DB. MOST PLURAL ASKS ARE CHECKED ACROSS THE WHOLE COLLECTION. sent_once_in_order (functional/judge.toml:213-217) requires JUDGE-D1 exactly once in the thread, search AND transcript. It also requires the C,A,B order in Harriet's and Gwen's threads, search and the transcript, which matches conversations.md:29 ('wherever you see them: the thread, search and the transcript'). search_and_transcript B2 (judge.toml:244) requires that 'each message shows its author and sent time'. safe_formatting (judge.toml:177) checks the thread, the reply quote, the search snippet and the transcript. edits_and_stale_edit (judge.toml:162) adds earlier versions, so all five places in conversations.md:13 are covered. hold_scope_and_release step 2 (judge.toml:146) checks the held child AND both its unheld parent and grandchild. wall_every_route and wall_mentions_and_links together cover the matter list, thread, search and snippets, transcript, replays, mentions and link-preview routes listed in walls-and-retention.md:59. The seed probes are unique across all matters (checked in seed_data.json): 'Probate', '2,400' and '4,200' appear only in K-13; 'Insurer letter' only in K-17; 'Fenwick' and 'heads of terms' only in M-12. 'JUDGE-O' and 'JUDGE-D1' are not substrings of any other probe. So the global 'finds nothing' searches (timer_changes step 2, hold step 6, deleted Part A/B) and the 'exactly once' counts are achievable, and a conforming app does not trip them. UNCHANGED GUARDS DO NOT PUNISH LEGITIMATE SIDE EFFECTS. Moving M-13 to 7 days deletes only K-13: K-7 is held, and K-8 (sent 05-10) stays, so message_links and live_updates still find 'Draft will sent for your review.'. The persistence 'unchanged' and 'exactly what they returned' checks (judge.toml:259, 263-264) compare against values noted just before restart_app, so the earlier deletions of K-13 and K-17 are tolerated. Gwen's unread count only has to be 'at least 2' (judge.toml:202), which allows for her earlier reads and posts. live_updates asks that the thread 'has not jumped to a different place', not for an exact scrollTop. prompt.md:47 and 72-76 and app_context.md:111 state the shared-state order. The scripted golden run (hashes verified) passed all 16 functional legs, gate_constraints and polish_refusal_in_place on one database across a real restart (functional-before.json and functional-after.json are all true). This is scripted evidence only: there is no configured judge run, no Oracle and no model score. DEFECT, primary instance. integration.md:42 is universal: 'Anyone who isn't signed in gets no matter, message, mention or transcript data from the server' (see also instruction.md:7). The only signed-out check is signin_and_client_scope Part A (judge.toml:44): 'replay that recorded request [the message-loading request]... it must return no matter, message or name data'. One sampled request stands in for four kinds of data. No criterion replays the mentions, search or matter-list request while signed out, and none opens a transcript address while signed out. wall_every_route step 4 (judge.toml:62) opens the transcript as Dev, who is signed in and walled, which is a different code path. gates/render (judge.toml:28-29) checks only what the UI shows before sign-in. Secondary instances (P3, Note level). (a) 'Only a partner' changes a timer and places or releases a hold, and 'Harriet' adds or lifts walls (walls-and-retention.md:61, 65, 71). These are refused only for associate Sian (timer step 5, hold steps 4 and 7, wall_added_live step 3). No client is ever tried, so a role check written as `role === 'associate' -> deny` passes. (b) 'Nobody can be mentioned in a matter they can't see' (conversations.md:21) is checked only for walled Dev, not for a client mentioned in a matter that is not theirs (for example @Paul in M-11). (c) 'Turning a timer off or lengthening it never brings anything back' (walls-and-retention.md:65) is checked after 'off' (timer step 3) but not after lengthening back to 30 days (step 4).
counterexample: A plausible broken app passes every criterion. It mounts app.use('/api', requireAuth), so GET /api/matters/:id is correctly protected. Its transcript page lives outside /api as GET /transcript/:id and checks only `if (req.user && isWalled(req.user, id)) return notAvailable()`, a wall check with no sign-in check. It also registers /api/mentions before the auth middleware. Signed out, fetch('/transcript/M-11') then returns the full M-11 transcript with names, message texts and hold marks. signin Part A still passes because only the message-loading request is replayed. wall_every_route step 4 still passes because Dev is signed in and walled. The render gate still passes because the sign-in page shows nothing. The app breaks integration.md:42 ('no ... mention or transcript data') yet gets full credit on the 2.0-weight criterion. In the other direction, I found no plural or unchanged check that would fail a conforming app, so this defect only over-credits.
suggested_fix: In signin_and_client_scope Part A, have the judge record three more things while signed in as Gwen: the M-11 transcript address, the mentions-list request and a search request. After sign-out, it replays each request and opens the transcript address, and every one must return no matter, message, mention or transcript data. Optionally, next to the existing Sian replays, add a client (Gwen) replay of the timer or hold request so the partner-only asks also cover non-associates.
